articles.summary: A mixed-methods systematic review in BMC Medical Education finds that extra time can level exam performance for medical students with specific learning disabilities, but accommodations alone leave real gaps. The authors call for a comprehensive, flexible approach, and AI tools may have a role.
articles.title: Medical Students With Specific Learning Disabilities Continue to Face Educational Hurdles

articles.summary: In the phase 3 RASolute 302 study presented at ASCO 2026, the RAS(ON) inhibitor daraxonrasib nearly doubled median overall survival versus chemotherapy (13.2 vs 6.6 months) in previously treated metastatic pancreatic cancer, with far fewer treatment discontinuations.
articles.title: Daraxonrasib Demonstrates Superiority Over Chemotherapy in Metastatic Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma

articles.summary: A propensity-matched analysis of more than 10,000 patients across seven solid tumors found that GLP-1 receptor agonists were associated with reduced metastatic progression, reaching statistical significance in four cancers. The authors call for randomized trials.
articles.title: GLP-1 RAs Associated With Reduced Progression in Some Cancers

articles.summary: An asynchronous e-learning module sharply improved internal medicine residents' confidence in interpreting ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, according to a study in BMC Medical Education, where the share who felt comfortable rose from 22.6% to 84.6%.
articles.title: Dedicated Module Useful in Helping Internal Physicians Interpret Ambulatory Blood Pressure Readings

articles.summary: AI is taking on a growing role in mental healthcare, helping clinicians personalize treatment, monitor outcomes, and cut documentation time, according to a review in the Annual Review of Clinical Psychology.
articles.title: How AI is Quietly Transforming Mental Healthcare

articles.summary: The Korean Association for the Study of Intestinal Diseases reached a Delphi consensus on diagnosing and managing acute colonic diverticulitis, offering region-specific, evidence-based guidance for a disease that is becoming more common in Asia.
articles.title: Korean Experts Make Series of Recommendations for Managing Acute Colonic Diverticulitis

articles.summary: A new study in JMIR Medical Education finds that uncertainty about generative AI — including threats to professional identity and job security — may be contributing to a decline in medical students' mental well-being.
articles.title: Generative AI Tools Potentially Associated With a Decline in Medical Students' Mental Well-Being

articles.summary: Research into AI in sleep medicine is yielding useful applications for insomnia, sleep-related breathing disorders, hypersomnolence, and parasomnias, according to a review in Respiratory Medicine, where AI is positioned to support rather than replace clinicians.
articles.title: Can AI Help Us Sleep Better? New Research Suggests It Can

articles.summary: AI can play a significant role in drug repurposing, identifying existing medicines that may work for new diseases, according to a review in the Annual Review of Medicine. Because these drugs are already approved, repurposing can be faster and cheaper than developing new ones.
articles.title: The Next Blockbuster Drug May Already Exist, and AI Knows Where to Look

articles.summary: A 29-year-old primigravida at term with a giant uterine fibroid and a transverse fetal lie developed uterine torsion. This case report details how the surgical team prepared for multiple scenarios and safely delivered via a posterior lower uterine segment incision.
articles.title: Case Report: Management of Large Uterine Fibroids Causing Uterine Torsion During Delivery
